text:
Zara N.: Hey team — need help with a messy admin thing. Baby was added to my partner's health plan by the hospital, but I need the kid on Redwood's plan retroactive to birth. Also our childcare costs spiked and I'm wondering if a Dependent Care FSA election change midyear is allowed as a qualifying life event (QLE). Finally, we're planning to extend my parental leave by 8 weeks unpaid and want to keep the temporary contractor for overlap. What forms and timelines do I need?

Sofia (People Ops): Sorry for the juggling, congrats on the new baby! Short answers: 1) yes we can do retro enrollment for newborns but need docs within 30 days for medical; 2) DC-FSA midyear change typically requires a QLE (birth counts) and proof; 3) unpaid extension + contractor overlap is OK; hiring ops can keep contractor, benefits eligibility stays based on your employment status.

Kam (Benefits): Hello Zara  for retro active enrollment: submit the Dependent Enrollment form: https://intranet.redwood/benefits/dependent-enroll and attach the hospital birth record + SSN when available and partner plan proof that baby was initially listed elsewhere. In practice we can retro enroll to birth date if docs are within 30 days, otherwise effective date may be later. Dental/vision often also need the birth certificate within 30 days.

Zara N.: If I only got the partner-plan paperwork today, is 30 days from birth or from when I gathered docs?

Kam (Benefits): It's 30 days from the date of birth per the carrier contract. If you're outside the 30-day window we'll file a carrier appeal; success is not guaranteed but we've had approvals for medical emergencies. Add a short explanation in the form and attach hospital notes.

Ari (Payroll): Payroll note on retro coverage: if benefits allow retro enrollment, any associated premium differences will be withheld/adjusted in payroll. If it's more than one payroll cycle's worth, we can amortize the deduction across N cycles — let benefits know if you prefer spread payments.

Zara N.: Got it. What about DC-FSA? I thought elections are fixed at open enrollment except for QLEs. Birth should qualify, right?

Kam (Benefits): Birth is a QLE. Submit the FSA change request here: https://intranet.redwood/benefits/fsa-qle and attach birth certificate or hospital record. Deadline to submit for a QLE is 30 days from event; elections will be effective per plan rules (usually retro to event date).

Zara N.: If I increase my FSA midyear, can I also claim retro childcare costs I already paid?

Kam (Benefits): Generally yes  eligible expenses incurred after the QLE/event date and after the election effective date are reimbursable. If the election is effective retro to birth, prior childcare costs during approved coverage window may be eligible; you'll submit receipts to the FSA vendor for reimbursement. We'll share specifics in the confirmation email.

Zara N.: For the unpaid extension: I plan to extend 8 weeks unpaid starting 2026-10-25. Will I keep health benefits if unpaid?

Sofia (People Ops): During unpaid extension you can continue benefits either via company-paid continuation (rare) or by electing COBRA-style employee-paid continuation. Benefits team will send options and costs. File a Leave Amendment form and choose "unpaid extension" so Benefits can send specific enrollment/COBRA info.

Devon (Hiring Ops): On the contractor: we can keep the temp on for the overlap. From hiring ops side, no headcount change while you're on approved leave/extension. If you plan to come back and transition work, let me know desired overlap weeks and we'll set the contractor end date accordingly.

Zara N.: Sweet. Any effect on equity/vesting, paid time off accrual, or performance timeline for the unpaid extension?

Sofia (People Ops): Paid parental leave counts as service for vesting; unpaid extension may pause service accruals unless pre-approved otherwise. PTO accrual while unpaid is paused. Performance review timing remains the same but managers often schedule a mid-point check-in; discuss with your manager. If you want a formal exception to continue accruals, flag it in the amendment and we'll escalate to Comp.

Ari (Payroll): If benefits premiums shift to employee-paid during unpaid time, payroll will set up post-tax deductions or invoice depending on your election. For retro premium adjustments (from retro enrollment) we'll coordinate timing with you.

policy-bot: Quick policy summary: "Birth of a child = QLE for benefits and FSA. Dependent enrollment docs due within 30 days. FSA midyear changes allowed for QLE with proof. Unpaid leave options: COBRA-style continuation or company discretion. See intranet policy: https://intranet.redwood/policies/leave-benefits."

Office-Admin: If you need an on-campus space for pumping when you return part-time, DM me dates and I'll reserve rooms. Also we can add your newborn to the family lactation priority list for the first month.

Zara N.: Thank you all! I'll submit Dependent Enrollment + FSA QLE forms today and file the Leave Amendment for the unpaid extension. One small ask  can Benefits start a carrier appeal preemptively since I'm right at day 29?

Kam (Benefits): Yes send the docs in the form and add "carrier appeal requested" in the notes. We'll escalate once we get the packet. Expect reply in 3 business days.

Sofia (People Ops): If anyone needs to chime in on timing with the manager, @Devon will coordinate the contractor overlap and I'll confirm leave amendment routing. Ping us if you want a templated email for the forms.

Zara N.: Filing now. Appreciate the quick help :heart:
_notes: Thread covers retro dependent enrollment after birth, Dependent Care FSA QLE midyear changes, unpaid extension and benefits continuation, contractor overlap for handoff, payroll premium adjustments, and process links and deadlines. Short Slack-style messages with action items and a carrier appeal path.
